description:
Hi! We are around 15-year-old students passionate about space, science, and exploring new ideas.

We enjoy sports, music, and learning new things. We speak English and Turkish.

Our main interest is astronaut health and making life on Mars safer and healthier.

We are looking for curious, creative, and motivated teammates who enjoy science, technology, and teamwork.

You don't need to be an expert. Just bring your curiosity, enthusiasm, and ideas!
summary:
SpaceDNA Guardian is a proposed health monitoring system designed for astronauts on missions to Mars. 

Our project focuses on tracking space radiation exposure, heart rate and sleep patterns through a dashboard.

The dashboard will show real-time health data. Help detect potential risks during long space missions.

We are also studying cell- DNA or cfDNA as a possible future biomarker for biological stress caused by radiation.

Our goal is to build a prototype using simulated data to support the health monitoring needs of astronauts.

It is important to note that SpaceDNA Guardian is a research concept and not a tested medical device.
details:
SpaceDNA Guardian is a project that focuses on protecting astronaut health during space missions especially trips to Mars.

Space radiation hurts cells and DNA. Astronauts also face problems, with sleep physical fitness and a lack of medical help.

We propose creating a health dashboard that brings together three key measurements: radiation exposure, heart rate and sleep length.

The prototype will use astronaut health data to show trends and point out possible health risks. The goal is to make complicated health data simpler for astronauts and mission doctors to grasp.

We also want to look at cell‑free DNA (cfDNA) as a future sign of biological stress. This idea is still experimental. Is not yet a proven medical test.

SpaceDNA Guardian blends space science, medicine and digital tech. The next step is to build and show a working prototype.
dataRefs: NASA Space Radiation and Human Health
